clue.text: Measure of acidity sustained by Scandinavian nymph

indicators.note: to be sustained by something is to be held up within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Dane is a native of Denmark
pH is the chemist's scale of acidity

explanation.surface: A water sprite from Norse legend keeping her pond's acidity steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scandinavian nymph' reads as one phrase, but the Scandinavian is the outer shell and only 'nymph' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is the nymph of Greek myth who escaped Apollo by turning into a laurel tree.

clue.text: Entice by plot

parts.note: by and at both mean next to, as in 'at the door'
a plot of land is a tract

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a scheme, which would suit enticing, but it is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw someone towards you, which is what enticing does.

clue.text: Heroin, smuggled by toy and game company, leads to gains (except for one side)

indicators.note: goods smuggled by someone are hidden inside their luggage, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Hasbro makes Monopoly and Transformers
H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: except for leaves something out, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: a win brings a gain, as in wins and losses
I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A drug ring using a toy maker, profitable for everyone but one party.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the definition: 'side' alone defines, while 'except for one' removes a letter from the word for leads to gains.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash browns, fried grated potato, are a common side dish at an American breakfast.

clue.text: Clarify enigmatic clue I see

indicators.note: something enigmatic is puzzling and jumbled, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
to see someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: A solver asking someone to explain a baffling clue, then announcing they get it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' reads as a cry of understanding; split it, and see means go out with.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make something clear by explaining it.

clue.text: Like an ostrich or piebald cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the word before it is scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Comparing a flightless bird with a patchy-coloured cuckoo, as if they were similar birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' sits among birds so it looks like one, but here it only means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich walks and runs on two legs, which is what bipedal describes.

clue.text: Obscure northward journey with Jan's follower?

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, the reverse of normal order

parts.note: a go can mean a trip or journey
February follows January

explanation.surface: A murky trip north in the weeks after January.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to cloud or confuse, making something obscure.

clue.text: Relentlessly question quiet official

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
an ump is an umpire, a sports official

explanation.surface: Grilling a soft-spoken referee.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to keep questioning them persistently to extract information.

clue.text: Death to start up again?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a formal word for dying
second, whimsical meaning: to undo ceasing, the prefix de- reversing a stop

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: read as de- plus cease, the word would mean to stop stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal or legal term for death, while de-cease playfully means to reverse a halt.

clue.text: New York intellectual cat is on the streetcar, singing

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
the El is the elevated railway in American cities
trilling is warbling, as a bird sings

explanation.surface: A cat riding a tram and singing as it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Trilling was a Columbia literary critic, a leading figure among the New York Intellectuals.

clue.text: Strict believer entertaining lady with New Testament elite

parts.note: something entertaining is fun
a dame is a lady
NT is the usual abbreviation
the A-list is the elite of celebrities

explanation.surface: A devout person charming a lady and the best-connected Bible readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like a container signal, but here it is an adjective meaning amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundamentalist holds rigidly to the literal truth of scripture, the strictest form of belief.

clue.text: Craft spun out very loudly? That's good enough

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion or shape, so the following letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A boat sent spinning while someone yells, then a shrug that it will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat being spun, but it is a verb telling you to fashion the next two words anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to snuff is an idiom for meeting the required standard, adequate if not brilliant.

clue.text: Testosterone-laden revolutionary seen around Czech borders

indicators.note: something seen around another thing encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Mao Zedong led China's communist revolution

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A swaggering rebel spotted hanging about the frontiers of the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressively masculine manner, the kind blamed on an excess of male hormone.

clue.text: Design a game, making a connection that is frequently severed

parts.note: to design something is to draw it
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game designer inventing a game about forming links that keep getting broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge links a castle to the outside world, and is raised, cutting that link, whenever danger threatens.

clue.text: Beware Latin grotto

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Latin imperative for beware, once a schoolboy warning cry
second meaning: a hollow in rock or a hillside

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word is spelt exactly like the English one, which is the whole trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin cave is the command to watch out, while the English word is a natural chamber in rock, like a grotto.

clue.text: Part of leaf surrounding rotten center

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page

indicators.note: rotten means decayed and broken down, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Botany talk: a section of a leaf around a decaying core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of leaf' wants to be the definition, but only 'Part' defines, and leaf is a book's page.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion or share of a whole, that is, a part of it.

clue.text: Initially, Muhammad Ali toasts zwieback or unleavened wafer…

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so only opening letters count

parts.note: the first letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: The boxer raising a glass to dry rusks, or perhaps to a cracker, with the ellipsis running on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Matzo is the flat unleavened bread eaten at Passover, a thin crisp cracker.

clue.text: …because lunch involves key preference for some travelers

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: as can mean because, as in 'as it rained'
to lunch is to eat
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue: the reason travellers' lunch matters, plus their favourite seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The island goes inside the first piece only, between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Many passengers on planes and trains prefer a seat by the gangway, for leg room and easy exit.

clue.text: Lush circles on a mountaintop, as it were

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, as is a sot
O is the circle-shaped letter, so several circles are Os
the top of a mountain is its peak

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering in circles at the summit of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: So to speak and as it were are interchangeable idioms, flagging a figure of speech.

clue.text: Plea to get 100 in midday quiz

indicators.note: in tells you to put one piece inside another

parts.note: noon is midday
C is the Roman numeral for 100
a quiz is a short test

explanation.surface: A student begging for full marks in a lunchtime test.
explanation.walkthrough: The 100 goes inside the midday word only; the quiz follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea of no contest (nolo contendere) in a US court accepts conviction without admitting guilt.

clue.text: Register California grad student record

parts.note: CA is the postal code for California
a TA, teaching assistant, is usually a graduate student
a log is a record

explanation.surface: Signing up a graduate student in a California university's records.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalog is a systematic list of items, which is what a register is.

clue.text: Desert natives cast headliner at outset of play

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a play opens with Act I

explanation.surface: Native desert dwellers cast to play the star in a production's opening scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast headliner' looks like the star of the show; read it as the head of the word cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are plants native to the deserts of the Americas, thriving where water is scarce.

clue.text: Rod, on the ball, embraces one wrong style of cooking

indicators.note: to embrace something is to hold it in your arms, so the outer piece holds the inner

parts.note: a cue is the rod used on the ball in pool or snooker
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A sharp man named Rod getting a cooking style wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name and 'on the ball' like praise; together they describe a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a characteristic style or manner of cooking, as in French cuisine.

clue.text: Stake in the heart of giantess

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the letters are found inside it

parts.note: the run of letters in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Driving a stake into a giant woman's heart, like a vampire hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' looks like a wooden stake in a vampire story; it is a gambling stake.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Slip on fragments, in some cases more than once — that'll kill you

indicators.note: fragments are broken pieces, so the words before it are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

parts.words: in some cases more than once
parts.note: some of those six letters are used twice, adding a second copy of four of them

explanation.surface: A warning that stepping on broken shards, sometimes repeatedly, could be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the fodder supplies only six different letters; the clue admits that four of them are used twice in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison pill is a capsule of lethal poison, carried by spies to take if captured.

clue.text: Black-and-white swimmers, stripping for cash

indicators.note: stripping peels off the outside layer, leaving the inner run of letters

parts.note: the phrase run together, with its outer letters peeled away

explanation.surface: Penguins, perhaps, doing a striptease for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas, killer whales, are ocean swimmers with striking black-and-white markings.

clue.text: Over the phone, conceal personality's evil side

indicators.note: what is said over the phone is only heard, so the spelling may differ from the sound

parts.note: to conceal is to hide

explanation.surface: Someone hiding the dark half of their character during a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's novella, Mr Hyde is the evil persona into which the respectable Dr Jekyll transforms.

clue.text: I dissent about large piece of dental work

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer pieces go round the inner one

parts.note: nay is a vote against
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A patient objecting to the size of the work a dentist proposes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlay is a filling made outside the mouth and cemented into a cavity in a tooth.

clue.text: Male in the beginning, or possibly the end?

indicators.note: in tells you to place one piece inside another

parts.note: the Creation is the beginning of the world in Genesis
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Musing on whether the first man came at the start of things or the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Adam 'in the beginning'; the beginning is the Creation itself, with the male letter put into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremation, burning a body after death, is one way a life's story ends, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Fierce female soldier retreats, breaking lock

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A tough woman soldier falling back after forcing a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is a female tiger, and the word is also used of a fiercely aggressive woman.

clue.text: Custodian to look back once more?

indicators.note: back says the whole phrase is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A guard, perhaps a museum attendant, glancing over their shoulder a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: To look once more is to re-peek; that whole word is then turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper is a person in charge of looking after something, such as a zoo or a museum.
